This row straddles two kits: Base64/hex encoding lives in util.Base64Helper (import { util } from '@kit.ArkTS'), while message digests (DigestUtils / MD5 / SHA) live in cryptoFramework.createMd (import { cryptoFramework } from '@kit.CryptoArchitectureKit'). Mapped to @kit.CryptoArchitectureKit because the digest half has no other home; Base64-only users should prefer @kit.ArkTS util.
IOUtils / FileUtils stream and file operations → @kit.CoreFileKit. Attested: import { fileIo } from '@kit.CoreFileKit' (openSync, readSync, mkdirSync, listFileSync).

Logging → hilog. Attested: import { hilog } from '@kit.PerformanceAnalysisKit' (debug, isLoggable). NOTE: this is a rough fit, not an equivalence — the Android library is a pluggable-backend logging facade (the app binds logback/log4j at deploy time); HarmonyOS has no facade/binding layer, so appenders, MDC and per-logger levels need real rework.
Runtime permission request/check → @kit.AbilityKit. Attested: import { abilityAccessCtrl } from '@kit.AbilityKit' (verifyAccessToken, checkAccessToken).
Runtime permission request/check → @kit.AbilityKit abilityAccessCtrl; same target as com.zoontek.rnpermissions.
Connectivity state and change callbacks → @kit.NetworkKit. Attested: import { connection } from '@kit.NetworkKit' (hasDefaultNet, getNetCapabilities, createNetConnection).
Flutter connectivity_plus → @kit.NetworkKit connection; same target as react-native-netinfo.

Zip archive create/extract → @kit.BasicServicesKit. Attested: import { zlib } from '@kit.BasicServicesKit' (compressFile, decompressFile). zlib has no per-entry API, so zip4j's entry-level manipulation and AES encryption have no direct counterpart.
Zip/unzip → @kit.BasicServicesKit zlib compressFile/decompressFile.

In-process pub/sub → @kit.BasicServicesKit. Attested: import { emitter } from '@kit.BasicServicesKit'. Rough fit rather than equivalence: emitter carries no counterpart to EventBus sticky events, subscriber priorities or ThreadMode dispatch, so those need rework.

FCM remote messaging → @kit.PushKit; matches the existing com.google.firebase.messaging row. NOTE: the @kit.PushKit token rests on existing mapping.json precedent (4 rows) and KIT_DOC_URLS, not on an index import statement — hmos_api_index.json attests no @kit.PushKit import.

Analytics events → @kit.PerformanceAnalysisKit, matching the existing com.google.firebase.analytics row. Attested: import { hiAppEvent } from '@kit.PerformanceAnalysisKit' (addWatcher) and import { hilog } from '@kit.PerformanceAnalysisKit'. Chosen over @kit.AnalyticsKit, which the index does not attest at all.

JSON parse/serialize → ArkTS. Attested: import { ArkTSUtils } from '@kit.ArkTS' (parse, stringify); the JS builtin JSON also covers most fastjson usage. Fastjson's JSONPath and TypeReference generics have no direct counterpart and need rework.

Icon-font rendering → @kit.ArkUI. Attested: registerFont, SymbolGlyph, fontFamily. Medium because there is no drop-in icon-font component: the HarmonyOS equivalent is a composition (registerFont plus Text with fontFamily, or SymbolGlyph), not a single API.
Secure credential storage → @kit.UniversalKeystoreKit. Attested: import { huks } from '@kit.UniversalKeystoreKit' (generateKeyItem, importKeyItem, exportKeyItem).

File read/write/download → @kit.CoreFileKit. Attested: import { fileIo } from '@kit.CoreFileKit' (openSync, readSync, mkdirSync, listFileSync). RNFS upload/download helpers map to @kit.BasicServicesKit request instead.
Conceal encrypted storage → @kit.CryptoArchitectureKit. Attested: import { cryptoFramework } from '@kit.CryptoArchitectureKit' (createCipher, createSymKeyGenerator, doFinal).
Conceal Android keychain half → @kit.CryptoArchitectureKit; same target as com.facebook.crypto. Key material itself belongs in @kit.UniversalKeystoreKit huks.
PDF viewing → @kit.PDFKit. Attested: import { pdfService } from '@kit.PDFKit' (PdfDocument, loadDocument).

Logging → hilog. Attested: import { hilog } from '@kit.PerformanceAnalysisKit' (debug, isLoggable). NOTE: rough fit, not equivalence — hilog is a platform log SINK, while SLF4J is a pluggable-backend FACADE whose whole purpose is that the app binds logback/log4j at deploy time. HarmonyOS has no facade/binding layer. org.slf4j.MDC and org.slf4j.helpers.* are exactly the parts that do not port; appenders and per-logger levels need real rework, not a symbol swap.

Cookie get/set/clear → @kit.ArkWeb. Attested: import { webview } from '@kit.ArkWeb' (configCookieSync, fetchCookieSync, saveCookieAsync). Cookies are managed by the web stack on HarmonyOS, not by @kit.NetworkKit.
Barcode/QR scanning → @kit.ScanKit. Attested: import { detectBarcode } from '@kit.ScanKit' (also generateBarcode, scanCore).

Barcode/QR decoding → @kit.ScanKit. Attested: import { detectBarcode } from '@kit.ScanKit' (also generateBarcode, scanCore). NOTE: this is a vendored ZXing copy bundled INSIDE the DCloud uni-app runtime. @kit.ScanKit is correct for the barcode-scanning capability itself, but the surrounding uni-app runtime is not separately mappable (Phase 2C classified io.dcloud/uts/com.dcloud as SKIP - a whole cross-platform runtime, not a library). Do not read this row as 'swap one library'.
Barcode detection → @kit.ScanKit. Attested: import { detectBarcode } from '@kit.ScanKit' (also generateBarcode, scanCore).
Biometric authentication → @kit.UserAuthenticationKit. Attested: import { userAuth } from '@kit.UserAuthenticationKit' (getUserAuthInstance, UserAuthType, AuthParam).

Fingerprint authentication → @kit.UserAuthenticationKit. Attested: import { userAuth } from '@kit.UserAuthenticationKit' (getUserAuthInstance, UserAuthType, AuthParam). The FingerprintCipher/FingerprintDialog split maps onto userAuth plus @kit.UniversalKeystoreKit huks for key binding.
PDF rendering core → @kit.PDFKit. Attested: import { pdfService } from '@kit.PDFKit' (PdfDocument, loadDocument).
PDF viewer component → @kit.PDFKit. Attested: import { pdfService } from '@kit.PDFKit' (PdfDocument, loadDocument).
Mask overlay → @kit.ArkUI. Attested: Mask, maskShape. No drop-in component exists: the HarmonyOS equivalent is a composition, not a one-for-one widget swap.
Checkbox control → @kit.ArkUI. Attested: Checkbox, CheckboxGroup — a direct component equivalent.
Date/time picker → @kit.ArkUI. Attested: showDatePickerDialog, DatePickerOptions (and showTimePickerDialog for the time variant).

Toolbar / app bar → @kit.ArkUI. Attested: Toolbar. No drop-in component exists: the HarmonyOS equivalent is a composition, not a one-for-one widget swap. ArkUI expresses this through the Navigation component's title bar and toolbar slots rather than a standalone Toolbar widget.
Pull-to-refresh → @kit.ArkUI. Attested: Refresh, a direct container equivalent. SmartRefresh's custom header/footer animations map onto Refresh's builder slots.

Splash screen → @kit.ArkUI window. Attested: setWindowLayoutFullScreen (import { window } from '@kit.ArkUI'). No drop-in component exists: the HarmonyOS equivalent is a composition, not a one-for-one widget swap. HarmonyOS has no splash-screen API as such; the launch experience is an ability-level start page plus window configuration.

Process relaunch → @kit.AbilityKit. Attested: terminateSelf (and process.exit from @kit.ArkTS). Medium because HarmonyOS exposes no true process-restart primitive — terminateSelf plus startAbility approximates it, with different lifecycle semantics.
App restart → @kit.AbilityKit terminateSelf plus startAbility; same caveat as com.jakewharton.processphoenix — there is no true process-restart primitive.
Location fixes and change callbacks → @kit.LocationKit. Attested: getCurrentLocation (import { geoLocationManager } from '@kit.LocationKit').
Calendar event CRUD → @kit.CalendarKit. Attested: import { calendarManager } from '@kit.CalendarKit' (getCalendarManager, addEvent).

SVG rendering → @kit.ImageKit, which accepts SVG as an image source (index key 'svg tags' resolves to import { image } from '@kit.ImageKit'). For programmatic path-level rendering the closer API is drawing.buildFromSVGString (import { drawing } from '@kit.ArkGraphics2D'); medium because AndroidSVG spans both roles.

Video playback → @kit.MediaKit. Attested: createAVPlayer (import { media } from '@kit.MediaKit'). The bundled ExoPlayer surface (com.brentvatne.exoplayer) is replaced by AVPlayer plus an ArkUI XComponent/Video surface.
Video transcoding / compression → @kit.MediaKit. Attested: createAVTranscoder (import { media } from '@kit.MediaKit').

Date/time, calendar systems and timezone data → @kit.LocalizationKit. Attested: import { i18n } from '@kit.LocalizationKit' (getTimeZone, getCalendar). Time4J is large — its calendar-system breadth exceeds i18n, so exotic calendars may need rework.
Screen keep-awake → @kit.BasicServicesKit. Attested: import { runningLock } from '@kit.BasicServicesKit' (RunningLockType).
Package name / version / build number → @kit.AbilityKit. Attested: import { bundleManager } from '@kit.AbilityKit' (getBundleInfoForSelf, getBundleInfo).

okio's core (Buffer, ByteString, Source/Sink, Utf8) → import { buffer } from '@kit.ArkTS'; Base64 is util.encodeSync / util.decodeSync (@kit.ArkTS). This row STRADDLES two further kits and a migrator will need both: okio.FileSystem / FileHandle / Path / ZipFileSystem are fileIo (@kit.CoreFileKit), and GzipSource / GzipSink / DeflaterSink / InflaterSource are zlib (@kit.BasicServicesKit, createGzip / inflate attested). Medium because of that three-way split, not because the target is uncertain.

Bolts Task / TaskCompletionSource are continuation chains; the HarmonyOS equivalent is the JS Promise plus import { taskpool } from '@kit.ArkTS' for worker dispatch. Medium deliberately: CancellationToken / CancellationTokenSource / CancellationTokenRegistration have no direct counterpart and need real rework, not a symbol swap.

Text measurement (line width, font height, baseline offset) → import { MeasureText } from '@kit.ArkUI'. Medium: ArkUI lays text out declaratively, so the measuring code around it is rewritten rather than ported.

Animated image decoding → import { image } from '@kit.ImageKit' (createImageSource, getFrameCount, createPixelMap). @kit.ImageKit decodes the frames but has no play / pause / seek control; when playback control is required see @ohos/gif-drawable in ohpm_mapping.json, the same call made for pl.droidsonroids.gif.

Trace sections → import { hiTraceMeter } from '@kit.PerformanceAnalysisKit' (startTrace, finishTrace). Medium for the same reason org.slf4j is: hiTraceMeter is a platform trace sink, and Systrace's async-flow ids (beginAsyncSection / endAsyncFlow) have no counterpart.

FlexboxLayout → ArkUI Flex / Row / Column containers. NOT attested in hmos_api_index.json, and cannot be: ArkUI containers are declarative built-ins rather than imported APIs, so a grep for Flex over the index's import statements returns zero. The basis is precedent — com.facebook.yoga, RN's own flexbox engine, is already @kit.ArkUI medium — stated here so the weaker footing is not forgotten.
Camera preview / capture → import { camera } from '@kit.CameraKit' (createCameraInput, createPreviewOutput, getSupportedCameras).

Google Mobile Ads → import { advertising } from '@kit.AdsKit'. Medium: banner / interstitial / rewarded formats exist on both sides, but the mediation layer and the UMP consent flow do not port. Seen in 1 of the 43 corpus apps — kept because the correspondence is exact.

A relocated copy of OkHttp bundled inside the DCloud/uni-app runtime -- identical API (OkHttpClient, HttpUrl, Interceptor, CertificatePinner), only the package was renamed. Maps exactly where okhttp3 does: import { http } from '@kit.NetworkKit' (createHttp), plus webSocket for the WebSocket half. NOTE the caveat that applies to every dc.* row: the uni-app runtime around it does not port, so this is accurate namespace attribution, not a promise that swapping this one library completes the migration.

The shaded twin of okio, same reasoning and same three-way straddle as the okio row: core buffers are import { buffer } from '@kit.ArkTS', the filesystem half is fileIo (@kit.CoreFileKit) and the compression half is zlib (@kit.BasicServicesKit).

The pre-4.x Apache HTTP client. Same target as the existing org.apache.http row: import { http } from '@kit.NetworkKit' (createHttp / request). Kept as its own row because the package root is org.apache.commons, which the org.apache.http prefix cannot reach.

HttpHeaders / HttpMessageConverter / HttpOutputMessage are the request-response abstraction under RestTemplate -> import { http } from '@kit.NetworkKit'. Medium and deliberately scoped to .http only: org.springframework.core, .util and especially .web.servlet are general framework and server-side code with no client-side counterpart, and are left unmapped.

Ktor's client stack -> import { http } from '@kit.NetworkKit' with import { webSocket } from '@kit.NetworkKit' for io.ktor.websocket. Medium because the row covers the whole io.ktor root: the client, http and websocket packages port, while io.ktor.serialization and io.ktor.util are Kotlin-idiomatic plumbing that is rewritten rather than swapped, and Ktor's server side has no place on a device.

A vendored Volley fork (MR_RequestQueue / MR_RetryPolicy / MR_CacheDispatcher mirror Volley's RequestQueue / RetryPolicy / CacheDispatcher) -> import { http } from '@kit.NetworkKit', the same target as the existing com.android.volley row. Medium rather than high because the request-queue, retry and disk-cache policy layers are app code that must be rebuilt on top of http, not API that NetworkKit provides.

The LOCAL AUDIO I/O HALF of WebRTC only. WebRtcAudioRecord -> audio.createAudioCapturer, WebRtcAudioTrack -> audio.createAudioRenderer, WebRtcAudioEffects (AEC / NS) -> audio.getAudioEffectMode / setAudioEffectMode, all from import { audio } from '@kit.AudioKit'. READ THE SCOPE: org.webrtc as a whole is deliberately NOT mapped -- PeerConnection, ICE/SDP negotiation, SRTP/DTLS and the RTP transport have no HarmonyOS counterpart and must be hand-rolled or replaced with a vendor RTC SDK. This row says the microphone and speaker path ports, nothing more.

The CAPTURE HALF of WebRTC only: CameraCapturer / Camera1Session / Camera2Session / CameraEnumerator -> import { camera } from '@kit.CameraKit' (createCameraInput, createPreviewOutput, getSupportedCameras). Same scope warning as org.webrtc.audio -- the RTC stack itself does not port, and the video encode path (HardwareVideoEncoder, AndroidVideoDecoder) is left unmapped because no encoder/decoder API is attested in hmos_api_index.json.
Sandbox and document file IO. `import { fileIo } from '@kit.CoreFileKit'`; docs-ref harmonyos-guides/application-framework/core-file-kit.
`import { geoLocationManager } from '@kit.LocationKit'`; docs-ref harmonyos-guides/application-services/location-kit.
Local notifications. `import { notificationManager } from '@kit.NotificationKit'`. Remote push is @kit.PushKit -- Expo bundles both behind one module, so a migrator using push needs that kit as well.
`import { webview } from '@kit.ArkWeb'` with the Web component.
Device and app constants. `import { deviceInfo } from '@kit.BasicServicesKit'`; app-level values come from bundleManager (@kit.AbilityKit).
`runningLock` -- docs-ref harmonyos-references/.../basic-services-kit/device-management/ohos-runninglock-runninglock.
`import { http } from '@kit.NetworkKit'`. See also @kit.RemoteCommunicationKit (rcp), which Huawei documents as an equally valid session-based HTTP client.

docs-ref harmonyos-references/application-framework/background-tasks-kit. medium: HarmonyOS separates short-term transient tasks, long-running tasks with a declared background mode, and deferred workScheduler jobs, so one Expo task definition becomes a choice between three mechanisms.

Bundled asset access maps to `resourceManager` -- docs-ref harmonyos-references/application-framework/localization-kit (20 files). medium: Expo assets can also be resolved at runtime over the network, which resourceManager does not do.
`registerFont` plus Text fontFamily. medium: no drop-in loader -- ArkUI registers a font family rather than returning a handle.
HarmonyOS declares a start window (startWindowIcon/startWindowBackground in the ability config) rather than exposing a hide() call. medium: the API shape does not survive; the behaviour does.
Status/navigation bar styling via the window manager -- `setWindowSystemBarProperties`, docs-ref arkui/arkts-api/window-manager.
Push token acquisition. `import { pushService } from '@kit.PushKit'`.
Device/token plumbing behind HMS push registration.
Huawei ID sign-in; docs-ref harmonyos-guides/application-services/account-kit.
`hiAppEvent`. Mapped for consistency with com.google.firebase.analytics, which this file already routes to @kit.PerformanceAnalysisKit rather than @kit.AnalyticsKit.

SafetyDetect is Device Security Kit on HarmonyOS -- docs-ref harmonyos-guides/system/security/device-security-kit: 'checks whether the device environment is secure, for example whether it has been jailbroken or is a non-real device'.
`import { http } from '@kit.NetworkKit'`.

Passkeys/FIDO2 -- docs-ref harmonyos-references/system/security/online-authentication-kit (32 files; FIDO, FIDO2, IIFAA, SOTER). medium because Credential Manager spans three things: passkeys here, password autofill via autoFillManager (@kit.AbilityKit), and federated sign-in via @kit.AccountKit which is Huawei-ID only. No single API replaces it.
The provider half of Credential Manager. Same split as android.credentials.

SafetyDetect answers the same question. v1 recorded 'no native attestation API', which the documentation contradicts. Note the shape inverts: RootBeer runs local heuristics in-process, SafetyDetect is a device/server attestation with a nonce -- a redesign of the check, not a symbol swap.
docs-ref harmonyos-references/ai/core-vision-kit has faceDetector (detection) and faceComparator (verification) as first-class API pages. v1 checked @kit.VisionKit, a DIFFERENT kit.
Joins the existing io.invertase.googlemobileads row. medium: ad formats and mediation adapters do not port, only the serve/display concept.
Same family as com.google.ads.
Consent collection for ads. On HarmonyOS the equivalent is the Ads Kit consent flow together with AppGallery Kit's privacy agreement management.
The worklet runtime split out of react-native-reanimated, which this file already maps to @kit.ArkUI. Same caveat: ArkUI animation is declarative, so worklet code is rewritten rather than ported.
WebP decoding is native -- docs-ref media/image-kit (9 reference + 8 guide files mention webp). Fresco's WebP shim has no counterpart because the format is supported directly.
`import { detectBarcode } from '@kit.ScanKit'`, matching the existing com.journeyapps.barcodescanner row.
Zoomable Fresco image view. medium: ArkUI's Image with gesture modifiers covers it, and @ohos/photoview is the OHPM alternative already recorded for com.github.chrisbanes.photoview.
Tiled large-image viewer; same family as photodraweeview.
Launcher badge count. `setBadgeNumber` -- docs-ref push-kit and notification-kit. Joins me.leolin.shortcutbadger.
Pager dots. ArkUI's Swiper has a built-in indicator, so the library disappears rather than porting.

Kotlin image loading (fetch, decode, memory/disk cache, display). Same row as com.bumptech.glide / com.squareup.picasso. `import { image } from '@kit.ImageKit'` (kits/@kit.ImageKit.d.ts) decodes; ArkUI Image loads a URL and caches. Coil's interceptor/fetcher pipeline and Compose AsyncImage have no drop-in -- rebuilt on Image + image.createImageSource. One prefix covers coil3 too.

Map display, camera, markers, gestures. Same row as com.mapbox (MapLibre is its open fork). `import { map, mapCommon, MapComponent } from '@kit.MapKit'` (harmonyos-guides/application-services/map-kit). Custom styles and raster tile overlays exist (map-creation/displaying-a-custom-map, drawing-on-a-map/tileoverlay); MapLibre style-spec vector sources do not -- the missing half. org.maplibre.geojson is a data model and stays unmapped.

SQLite ORM. Storage is `import { relationalStore } from '@kit.ArkData'` (kits/@kit.ArkData.d.ts), like androidx.room. Annotation-driven entities and DAOs have no counterpart: RdbPredicates + ValuesBucket by hand.

Encrypted key-value store. Key-value half is `import { preferences } from '@kit.ArkData'` (kits/@kit.ArkData.d.ts), like android.content.SharedPreferences. Hawk encrypts every value; preferences does not -- secrets belong in @kit.AssetStoreKit instead.

UUID generation. `util.generateRandomUUID` / `generateRandomBinaryUUID` (api/@ohos.util.d.ts, re-exported by kits/@kit.ArkTS.d.ts) -- RFC 4122 version 4 only. JUG's time-based (v1/v6/v7) and name-based (v3/v5) generators have no counterpart.
Rounded / oval image with border. ArkUI Image takes `.borderRadius()` and `.border()` (component/common.d.ts), so the library disappears rather than porting.
Loading spinners. ArkUI `LoadingProgress` (component/loading_progress.d.ts) is one style; AVI's 28 animated styles are custom animation work.
Tooltip popups with arrows. ArkUI `.bindPopup(show, PopupOptions | CustomPopupOptions)` (component/common.d.ts). Balloon's overlay highlight and show-once persistence are not built in.
Slow pan-and-zoom over an image. ArkUI Image with animateTo on scale/translate; no built-in Ken Burns transition generator.
Snap-to-item scrolling for Compose lazy lists. ArkUI `List.scrollSnapAlign(ScrollSnapAlign)` (component/list.d.ts) does the core work; Snapper's custom fling behaviours do not carry over.
Swipe-to-act backgrounds on list rows. ArkUI `ListItem.swipeAction(SwipeActionOptions)` (component/list_item.d.ts) with start/end builders.
Horizontal/vertical pager for Compose. ArkUI `Swiper` (component/swiper.d.ts), indicator built in. Mapped per module like Expo: accompanist is a grab-bag.
Wrapping row/column layout for Compose. ArkUI `Flex({ wrap: FlexWrap.Wrap })` (component/flex.d.ts).

Draws an Android Drawable in Compose. ArkUI Image accepts a `DrawableDescriptor` / `PixelMapDrawableDescriptor` (api/@ohos.arkui.drawableDescriptor.d.ts, exported by @kit.ArkUI). Animated drawables need AnimatedDrawableDescriptor.

Bitmap transformations for Picasso (blur, grayscale, colour filter, crop, mask). `effectKit.createEffect(pixelMap)` with blur/brightness/grayscale/invert/setColorMatrix (api/@ohos.effectKit.d.ts, exported by kits/@kit.ArkGraphics2D.d.ts); crop is PixelMap.crop in @kit.ImageKit. Shape masks and GPU filter chains are hand work.

Local object database. Storage is `import { relationalStore } from '@kit.ArkData'` (kits/@kit.ArkData.d.ts), as androidx.room. Realm's live objects, schema migrations and Atlas Device Sync have no counterpart. @ohos/realm-core exists but is only the C++ core, not an SDK - pointing at it would overstate it.

RN camera module: preview, capture, recording. `import { camera } from '@kit.CameraKit'` (createCameraInput, createPreviewOutput). Its barcode half is @kit.ScanKit and face detection is @kit.CoreVisionKit, as org.reactnative.facedetector already is.
The older react-native-camera module; same row as org.reactnative.camera.
Page routing. ArkUI Navigation + NavPathStack (component/navigation.d.ts), as androidx.navigation. ARouter's annotation-generated route table, interceptors and service discovery are not built in.

Map display, camera, overlays -> `import { map, mapCommon, MapComponent } from '@kit.MapKit'`. The data is Petal Maps, not AMap's. AMap publishes its own HarmonyOS SDK, @amap/amap_lbs_map3d (publisher 高德开放平台), for an app that must stay on AMap data and keys.
Positioning -> `geoLocationManager` (kits/@kit.LocationKit.d.ts). AMap's own HarmonyOS SDK is @amap/amap_lbs_location (publisher 高德开放平台) when AMap coordinates/services are required.

POI search, geocoding, routing -> `import { site } from '@kit.MapKit'` (harmonyos-guides/application-services/map-kit/place-search). AMap's own HarmonyOS SDK is @amap/amap_lbs_search (publisher 高德开放平台).

Push delivery -> `import { pushService } from '@kit.PushKit'` (harmonyos-guides/application-services/push-kit). Getui's targeting backend is the vendor's: its HarmonyOS SDK is @getui/push (publisher getui), which itself rides on Push Kit.
Push delivery -> `import { pushService } from '@kit.PushKit'`. JPush's own HarmonyOS SDK is @jg/push (publisher 极光推送), on Push Kit. cn.jiguang (shared core/analytics) is not claimed.

On-device inference. `mindSporeLite.loadModelFromFile` (api/@ohos.ai.mindSporeLite.d.ts, exported by kits/@kit.MindSporeLiteKit.d.ts); ONNX models are converted offline to .ms (harmonyos-guides/ai/mindspore-lite-kit/using-mindspore-lite-for-model-conversion), and the supported operators are listed against ONNX Opset 18 (appendix/mindspore-lite-kit-operator-list). Same row as org.tensorflow.lite. No runtime ONNX loading; operators outside the list block conversion. @ohos/onnxruntime exists but native-first rules it out.

Form Kit covers the widget provider side (lifecycle via FormExtensionAbility, updates via formProvider), but widget hosting is open only to system apps. Evidence: `import { FormExtensionAbility } from '@kit.FormKit';` (data/harmonyos-references/application-framework/form-kit/arkts-apis/ohos-app-form-formextensionability-formextensionability/document.md); `Widget host: an application that displays the widget content and controls the widget location. Only the system application can function as a widget host.` (data/harmonyos-guides/application-framework/form-kit/arkts-widget-development-recommended/arkts-widget-overview/document.md). From v3 class-level mapping (partial: 1 of 4 used classes have a full equivalent; citations verified verbatim against docs-ref, reviewed 2026-10-13).

Self-managed VoIP calls (incoming and outgoing reports, call state, mute/speaker, failure causes) map to Call Service Kit voipCall. Telecom features such as phone accounts, call screening and InCallService (the default-dialer role) have no documented third-party equivalent. Evidence: `import { voipCall } from '@kit.CallServiceKit';` (data/harmonyos-references/application-services/call-service-kit/arkts-api/voipcall-in-app-call-management/document.md); `This module provides in-app call management functions, including reporting incoming and outgoing calls and call status to the system, as well as obtaining user touch events.` (data/harmonyos-references/application-services/call-service-kit/arkts-api/voipcall-in-app-call-management/document.md). From v3 class-level mapping (partial: 0 of 19 used classes have a full equivalent; citations verified verbatim against docs-ref, reviewed 2026-10-13).

ArkUI has no dedicated Card container, but any container (Column/Stack) gets CardView's rounded corners and elevation shadow from the universal borderRadius and shadow attributes; compat padding and corner-overlap prevention have no direct equivalent. Evidence: `borderRadius(value: Length | BorderRadiuses | LocalizedBorderRadiuses): T` (data/harmonyos-references/application-framework/arkui/arkts-components/universal-attributes/layout-and-borders/border-styling/document.md); `Applies a shadow effect to the component.` (data/harmonyos-references/application-framework/arkui/arkts-components/universal-attributes/visual-effects/image-effect/document.md). From v3 class-level mapping (partial: 0 of 1 used classes have a full equivalent; citations verified verbatim against docs-ref, reviewed 2026-10-13).

ArkUI covers custom views through FrameNode onDraw custom drawing and custom component layout (onMeasureSize/onPlaceChildren), but customview helpers such as ViewDragHelper, ExploreByTouchHelper and AbsSavedState have no one-to-one ArkUI equivalent, so this is partial. Evidence: `Implements custom drawing for the FrameNode. This API overrides the default drawing behavior and is invoked during FrameNode content rendering.` (data/harmonyos-references/application-framework/arkui/arkts-api/ui/arkui/framenode/document.md); `A custom component is considered to have a custom layout when either of the **onMeasureSize** or **onPlaceChildren** methods is implemented.` (data/harmonyos-references/application-framework/arkui/arkts-components/custom-components/custom-component-layout/document.md). From v3 class-level mapping (partial: 1 of 7 used classes have a full equivalent; citations verified verbatim against docs-ref, reviewed 2026-10-13).

ArkUI's built-in state management (state variables as ViewModel, bidirectional binding, @Observed, @Watch) does what data binding does, but it uses language decorators instead of generated binding classes and XML binding expressions, so the bindings must be rewritten. Evidence: `The UI development mode of ArkUI is the MVVM mode. State variables play the role of ViewModel in the MVVM mode.` (data/harmonyos-guides/application-framework/arkui/ui-development-arkts-based-declarative-development-paradigm/ui-paradigm-state-management/mvvm-v1/document.md); `Bidirectional binding: Views are bound to ViewModel data to implement bidirectional synchronization.` (data/harmonyos-guides/application-framework/arkui/ui-development-arkts-based-declarative-development-paradigm/ui-paradigm-state-management/mvvm-v1/document.md). From v3 class-level mapping (partial: 0 of 21 used classes have a full equivalent; citations verified verbatim against docs-ref, reviewed 2026-10-13).

ArkData preferences provides persistent key-value storage (get/put/delete/clear/getAll/flush/on change) covering Preferences DataStore, but typed-serializer DataStores, multi-process DataStores, corruption handling and SharedPreferences migration have no documented equivalent. Evidence: `import { preferences } from '@kit.ArkData';` (data/harmonyos-references/application-framework/arkdata/arkts-apis/ohos-data-preferences-user-preferences/document.md); `The **Preferences** module provides APIs for processing data in the form of key-value (KV) pairs, including querying, modifying, and persisting KV pairs.` (data/harmonyos-references/application-framework/arkdata/arkts-apis/ohos-data-preferences-user-preferences/document.md). ArkUI's SideBarContainer in Overlay mode shows or hides a sidebar over the content area, which is the drawer's core job. The docs show no edge-swipe drawer gesture, no scrim color and no lock modes, so those must be built by hand. Leanback is a prebuilt TV browse/details/search UI framework; ArkUI gives the building blocks (Grid, List, Search, LazyForEach data sources, arrow-key focus navigation, shared element transitions), but no ready-made browse, details, card, or background-manager screens were found, so those screens would have to be rebuilt. Space maps directly to the ArkUI Blank spacer; for WakefulBroadcastReceiver only the wake-lock half has a match (runningLock), and its broadcast-starts-service pattern does not. Evidence: `import {runningLock} from '@kit.BasicServicesKit';` (data/harmonyos-references/system/basic-functions/basic-services-kit/arkts-apis/device-management/ohos-runninglock-runninglock/document.md); `The **Blank** component is a spacer in the layout, automatically filling the remaining space along the main axis of its parent container.` (data/harmonyos-references/application-framework/arkui/arkts-components/blank-and-divider/blank/document.md). HarmonyOS has no lifecycle-managed Loader framework; TaskPool in @kit.ArkTS covers the background-load-and-cancel part, while LoaderManager retention and the CursorLoader content query have no documented counterpart. Evidence: `You can use the TaskPool APIs to create background tasks and perform operations on them, for example, executing or canceling a task.` (data/harmonyos-references/application-framework/arkts/arkts-apis/ohos-taskpool-starting-the-task-pool/document.md); `import { taskpool } from '@kit.ArkTS';` (data/harmonyos-references/application-framework/arkts/arkts-apis/ohos-taskpool-starting-the-task-pool/document.md). LocalBroadcastManager does in-process publish/subscribe of events, and the emitter module in @kit.BasicServicesKit provides the same thing: on/off/emit for events inside a process. Evidence: `The **Emitter** module provides the capabilities of sending and processing inter- or intra-thread events in a process.` (data/harmonyos-references/system/basic-functions/basic-services-kit/arkts-apis/process-and-thread-communication/ohos-events-emitter-emitter/document.md); `import { emitter } from '@kit.BasicServicesKit';` (data/harmonyos-references/system/basic-functions/basic-services-kit/arkts-apis/process-and-thread-communication/ohos-events-emitter-emitter/document.md).
